layers.name: Important Wetlands
layers.goal: Avoid any development, clearing, filling or drainage in the wetlands Vermont has mapped as state-significant.
layers.motivation: Wetlands the town cannot replace: rare types such as the intermediate fen at Gillette Swamp, the wet clayplain forest at Connant Swamp and the sugar maple floodplain forest at Post Mills, plus the best examples of more common ones. Rare wetlands depend on particular soils, water chemistry and groundwater flow that can't be rebuilt once disturbed, so the aim is avoidance, not careful use. Vermont tracks them through its Natural Heritage Inventory.
how_built: Start with State-Significant Wetland Communities (Natural Heritage), buffered 50 ft

layers.name: Second Tier Crossings
layers.goal: Keep the town's remaining road crossings permeable where habitat continues on both sides.
layers.motivation: The full set of wildlife crossings identified in the town inventory. Crossings that also fall inside the regional connectivity network appear in the top tier as well, and the map shows each area at its highest tier. Individually lower stakes, but collectively they are what keeps the town permeable at a local scale by letting animals reach feeding, breeding and overwintering habitat within Thetford rather than only through it. From the 2025 Thetford wildlife road crossing study.

Keep each whole feature that comes within 100 ft of Forest Connectivity Blocks, where priority is highest or priority
Buffer the result 100 ft

layers.name: Deer Wintering Areas
layers.goal: Keep the softwood cover that deer depend on in winter intact and connected.
layers.motivation: Deer wintering areas are the patches of dense softwood (hemlock, balsam fir, red spruce or white pine) where white-tailed deer gather when snow is deep. Near the northern edge of the species' range, these yards decide whether deer get through hard winters, so Vermont treats them as important wildlife habitat under Act 250 and other regulations. Losing the softwood canopy, or cutting the travel lanes between yards, can make an area useless for wintering deer for decades (VT Fish & Wildlife, Deer Wintering Areas).
how_built: Start with Deer Wintering Areas
